intro: What to install for this trip and what each app is for. Set up the must-haves at home: most of them send an SMS code to your phone number when you sign up.

items.name: Grab: Taxi Ride, Food Delivery
items.what: Main ride app in Phuket. Cars and motorbike taxis, with the price shown before you book. 2026 guides say it is the only ride app with an official pickup point at Phuket airport.
items.where: Phuket: whole island, incl. the airport. Natai (Phang Nga): yes, since Mar 2025. Koh Samui: yes. Koh Phangan: no, there are no or almost no Grab drivers.
items.setup: Install at home and sign up with your own phone number. Grab sends a code by SMS, so do it while your home SIM works. Add a credit or debit card. No Thai SIM needed.
items.cost: Free app. Fares shown before you book. Advance Booking adds a fee, about 50 baht for GrabCar (2026 guide).
tips: Airport, international arrivals: go out at Exit 8 and walk toward the domestic terminal to the Grab pickup point. Domestic: exit at Gate 1, turn right to the Grab booth.
Ride types at Phuket airport: JustGrab (nearest car or taxi), GrabCar, GrabCar Premium, GrabBike, and GrabSUV or GrabCar Plus for more space and luggage.
Advance Booking: book from 90 days up to 75 minutes before pickup, at a fixed price. Use it for the ride to the airport on 26 Jan.
Safety: tap 'Share my ride' so a friend can follow your car live. The emergency button alerts help. The in-app chat translates your messages.
GrabBike is a motorbike taxi for one person. Legal riders have yellow number plates. You must wear the helmet.
2026 guides: about 600-950 baht from the airport to Patong and 250-380 from Patong to Kamala. Prices go up at busy times and in heavy rain.
Grab works in all of Phang Nga since Mar 2025, so you can book rides to and from Baba Beach Club in Natai. Pay by card or cash.
Foreign visitors can buy a Grab Travel Pass for Thailand in the app (Account > Subscription). The vouchers last 4 weeks from the day you buy. Check the price first.
The same app orders food (GrabFood) in Phuket. Grab does not work on Koh Phangan: for food there, use Delivery KPG.

items.name: Bolt: Request a Ride
items.what: Second ride app. Often cheaper than Grab, so compare both before each ride. Has XL and Van cars for groups of up to 6.
items.where: Phuket. At Phuket airport only drop-offs at the terminal; for pickups you walk out of the airport gate. Koh Phangan: no. Koh Samui and Natai: not confirmed.
items.setup: Install at home and sign up with your phone number and the code it sends. Add a card, but also carry cash.
items.cost: Free app. Fares shown before you book.
tips: 2026 guides say Bolt is often 5-30% cheaper than Grab in Phuket. Check both apps.
Bolt drivers cannot pick up at the airport terminal. They wait outside the airport gate, a 5-10 minute walk with bags.
Bolt's Thai licence ran out in May 2026. In July it still ran on a temporary permit while the Land Transport Department decides. Keep Grab ready.
In early Sep 2026 Bolt briefly paused rides in Thailand to update driver records. Check that the app finds cars before you rely on it.
Card payment works, but many Phuket drivers prefer cash. Carry small notes.
Phuket ride types: Economy, Bolt, XL and Van (up to 6 people), and Taxi. You can schedule a ride from 30 minutes to 90 days ahead.
Safety: the Emergency Assist button, and 'Share location' sends your car and live position to a friend.

items.name: inDrive: rides at your price
items.what: Ride app where you offer your own price and drivers accept or counter. Often the cheapest, but fewer drivers and mostly cash.
items.where: Phuket, best in Rawai, Chalong, Kata and central Patong. No pickups inside Phuket airport. Koh Phangan: no. Koh Samui: not confirmed.
items.setup: Optional. Install at home and sign up with your phone number. Carry cash.
items.cost: Free app. You offer the fare.
tips: Type your price; drivers accept it or ask for more. Choose a driver by rating, car and arrival time.
It works in Phuket in 2026, but has fewer drivers than Grab. Outside the busy areas nobody may take your offer.
Most drivers want cash, and cancellations before pickup are common. Use Grab when time matters.
Drivers cannot pick you up inside Phuket airport.

items.name: Maxim: order a taxi & delivery
items.what: Another ride app that lists Phuket and Ko Samui. Shows the price before you order. Only a backup when Grab and Bolt find no car.
items.where: Phuket and Koh Samui (Maxim's city list). Not on Koh Phangan. Airport pickups: not confirmed.
items.setup: Optional. Install at home and sign up with your phone number.
items.cost: Free app. Price shown before you order.
tips: On the Land Transport Department's list of certified ride apps (June 2026).
Pay by cash or card (store listing).
There are few traveller reviews from Phuket, so it is not confirmed how many drivers it has. Try it only when the other apps fail.

items.name: Phuket airport taxi and limousine counters
items.what: Official counters at Phuket airport: fixed-price limousine cars and minibuses, metered taxis and shared minibuses. Easy for the big group on 8 Jan.
items.where: Phuket airport (HKT), both terminals, right after the arrivals exit. Rides to all of Phuket, and to Natai and other provinces.
items.setup: Optional: book a fixed-price car or a minibus for the group online before the flight.
items.cost: Car (up to 3): Nai Yang 400, Kamala 750, Patong 800 baht. Minibus (up to 10): Kamala 1,300. Taxi: meter + 100 baht.
tips: Phuket Airport Limousine has counters at the domestic exit Gate 1 and the international exit Gate 2. Prices are fixed and shown before you pay.
Prices on its website (Oct 2026), car for up to 3: Phuket Town 650, Kamala 750, Patong 800, Kata 1,000 baht. SUV for 4 (07:00-18:00 only): Kamala 1,100.
Minibus for 5-10 people: Nai Yang 600, Kamala 1,300, Patong 1,400 baht. Pay online by card, PromptPay or e-wallet, or at the counter.
Metered taxis wait outside the terminal at the 'Metered Taxi' sign. You pay the meter plus a 100-baht airport fee.
Shared minibus (P.M.K. counter), per person: 150 baht to Phuket Town, 180 to Patong, 200 to Kata or Rawai (official airport list).
EVme electric VIP taxis: counter in the domestic terminal, level 1, Public Transport Center. Meter from 150 baht plus the 100-baht airport fee.

items.name: Phuket Smart Bus
items.what: Cheap bus along the west coast: Airport - Surin - Kamala - Patong - Karon - Kata - Rawai for 100 baht. Live bus map on the website. No app needed.
items.where: Phuket only. Route 1 starts outside the domestic terminal at HKT (Exit 3) and stops in Kamala. No stop in Nai Yang. Not on Koh Samui or Koh Phangan.
items.setup: Nothing to install. Bookmark the live map (phuketsmartbus.com/tracking). Have a contactless card or small notes.
items.cost: Route 1: 100 baht flat. Route 2: 50 baht. Dragon Line: free. Route 1 pass: 299 baht for 1 day, 799 for 7 days.
tips: From the airport every 30 minutes, 08:15-23:30. Last bus from Rawai to the airport 19:30. Times change with traffic.
Airport to Kamala takes about 50 minutes. Kamala to the airport: first bus about 06:15, last about 20:35 (Big C Kamala), about 1 hour 15 minutes.
At the airport: go out at Exit 3 of the domestic terminal, turn left and follow the public transport walkway to the blue Smart Bus sign.
Pay on board: tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard or JCB card, Apple Pay or Google Pay, or pay cash. The QR is for Thai bank apps (PromptPay).
Route 2 runs Bus Terminal 2 - Phuket Town - Patong (50 baht). The Dragon Line in Old Town is free.
Help: LINE @pksb or WhatsApp +66 86 306 1257.
The Android app called 'Phuket Smart Bus' is unofficial. Use the website instead.

items.name: Koh Phangan songthaews and taxis (no app)
items.what: Ride apps do not work reliably on Koh Phangan. You use shared songthaew pickup trucks, private taxis and taxi boats. Always agree the price before you get in.
items.where: Koh Phangan only: Thong Sala pier, Ban Tai, Haad Rin and the party venues.
items.setup: Nothing to install. Ask your Ban Tai hotel for a driver's WhatsApp or LINE before you arrive.
items.cost: Shared truck about 200 baht per person from Thong Sala to Haad Rin (2026 guides); more late at night and on party nights.
tips: Do not count on Grab, Bolt or inDrive here: there are no or almost no drivers.
Songthaews wait at Thong Sala pier, mostly when boats arrive. Tell the driver where you go and agree the price per person.
Save the number of a good driver on day one, or ask your hotel to call one. Private taxis cost more than shared trucks.
Trucks get rare after dark. On Full Moon night they run through the night, but prices go up and they fill up fast. Plan the ride home.
Taxi boats serve beaches on the north and east coast.
Easier arrival: Lomprayah and Seatran sell boat tickets with a van to your Koh Phangan hotel (not Thong Nai Pan), 670-700 baht from Samui airport.
items.verification: 16 Oct 2026: maratnomad.com (updated 20 Mar 2026) says ride apps do not operate there; fullmoonparty.guide says coverage is patchy and unreliable; goasia.cc (updated 16 Oct 2026) covers night service, Full Moon prices and water taxis. Hotel-van fares from the Lomprayah and Seatran booking systems for 19 and 23 Jan 2027.

items.name: Lomprayah
items.what: Big ferry company for Samui and Koh Phangan. Van + fast boat from Samui airport to Thong Sala, and back. Book on the website; there is no app.
items.where: Samui airport (van to Bangrak pier) and Bangrak pier to Thong Sala pier on Koh Phangan. Also bus + boat tickets from Phuket.
items.setup: Book on lomprayah.com at home. Save the e-ticket email on your phone so you can open it offline.
items.cost: Samui airport to Thong Sala 500 baht. Thong Sala to Bangrak pier 350 baht. Samui airport to or from your Koh Phangan hotel 700 baht (booking site, Jan 2027).
tips: 19 Jan 2027, Samui airport to Thong Sala: about every hour from 07:30 to 15:00, last at 17:00. The trip takes about 1 hour.
23 Jan 2027, Thong Sala to Samui airport: 07:30, 10:45, 12:30, 13:40, 14:00 and later. The 10:45 is at the airport at 11:30, so it fits an afternoon flight.
Hotel ticket: a van picks you up at your Koh Phangan hotel (not Thong Nai Pan). On 23 Jan the 09:30 pickup is at Samui airport at 11:30. 700 baht.
On 16 Oct 2026 some boats showed only 2-5 seats left online. Book early for the full-moon week.
Be at the Lomprayah counter 60 minutes before departure to confirm your trip (Lomprayah terms).
Tickets cannot be refunded. One date change is free if you email at least 2 days before. 20 kg of luggage is free; more costs 200 baht.
Lost the email? Open 'My bookings' on lomprayah.com. Enter your email and ticket code, or get a 6-digit code by email, to show your ticket.
Help: phone or WhatsApp 065 350 9040 (08:00-20:00), LINE @pnd0714w.
items.verification: 16 Oct 2026: no Lomprayah app in the App Store (US, TH) or Google Play search. Times, prices and online seats for 19 and 23 Jan 2027 pulled from the lomprayah.com booking system and matched to its 2026 PDF timetable. Terms updated 14 May 2026; contacts from the timetable page.

items.name: Seatran Discovery
items.what: Second ferry company from Samui to Koh Phangan, with vans from Samui airport. Use it when Lomprayah times or seats do not fit.
items.where: Check-in counters at Samui airport (Smack One counter), Bangrak pier (Samui) and Thong Sala pier (Koh Phangan).
items.setup: If you use it, book on seatrandiscovery.com or 12Go at home and save the booking on your phone.
items.cost: Samui airport to Thong Sala 500 baht; Thong Sala to Bangrak pier 350 baht; Samui airport to your Koh Phangan hotel 670 baht (booking site, Jan 2027).
tips: Samui airport to Thong Sala on 19 Jan 2027: 07:30, 09:00, 12:00 and 14:00. The trip takes 1 to 1.25 hours.
Thong Sala to Samui airport on 23 Jan 2027: 10:30 and 11:00 (at the airport 12:00 or 12:30), then 16:00 and 16:45.
No app in the stores. Help: LINE Official, ebooking@seatrandiscovery.com, +66 86 476 4825.
items.verification: 16 Oct 2026: no Seatran app in the App Store or Google Play search. Times and prices for 19 and 23 Jan 2027 pulled from the route search on seatrandiscovery.com; check-in places and contacts from its check-in page.

items.name: Haad Rin Queen
items.what: Boat straight from its own pier in Bangrak on Samui to Haad Rin, the Full Moon beach. Slow ferry or fast speedboat. Book on its website.
items.where: Its own pier in Bangrak on Koh Samui, close to the airport, and Haad Rin pier on Koh Phangan.
items.setup: Optional. Book on haadrinqueen.com (Thai or English) or buy at the pier.
items.cost: Ferry 200 baht, speedboat 500 baht (booking site, Jan 2027).
tips: Haad Rin to Samui on 19 and 23 Jan 2027: ferry 09:30 and 16:00 (50 min), speedboat 12:30 and 17:00 (25 min).
Samui to Haad Rin: ferry 10:30 and 17:00, speedboat 15:00 and 18:30. The 18:30 is the latest boat to Koh Phangan we found on these days.
Online booking closes 30 minutes before each boat.
Its Samui pier is not the Seatran pier, so open the pin on haadrinqueen.com. It is close to Samui airport; take a taxi or Grab.
items.verification: 16 Oct 2026: no app in the App Store or Google Play search. Times, prices, seats and the 30-minute booking cut-off for 19 and 23 Jan 2027 pulled from the haadrinqueen.com schedule search; pier pins and office hours from its site.

items.name: 12Go Train Bus Ferry Flight
items.what: Booking app for ferries, buses, vans, transfers and flights in Thailand, incl. Phuket to Koh Phangan routes. Good to compare times and operators.
items.where: Online. Covers Phuket, Koh Samui and Koh Phangan routes (Lomprayah, Seatran and others).
items.setup: Install at home and make an account. After booking, save the PDF voucher on your phone (offline).
items.cost: Free app. Ferry tickets can cost about 50-100 baht more than on the operator's own site.
tips: Look for the 'e-ticket' sign on the trip. Then the PDF on your phone is enough. Without it, print the voucher or swap it for a ticket at the counter.
Compare the price with Lomprayah and Seatran's own sites before you pay.
Check the pier name: Samui has several piers (Bangrak, Nathon, Maenam/Pralarn). Also check the check-in place and time on your voucher.
Pay by card (3D Secure), PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay or PromptPay. If something goes wrong on the trip, call the phone number on your voucher.

items.name: Bangkok Airways
items.what: Airline app for your Phuket - Samui flights: booking, online check-in and the boarding pass on your phone. Also shows where the airline's lounges are.
items.where: Phuket airport (domestic terminal) and Samui airport, which Bangkok Airways owns.
items.setup: Install at home and open your booking in the app. Check in from 24 hours before each flight and save the boarding pass.
items.cost: Free app.
tips: Online check-in opens 24 hours and closes 1 hour before departure, in the app or on the website.
The boarding pass on your phone is accepted at security and at the gate.
Domestic check-in counters close 40 minutes before departure. Drop your bags at least 30 minutes before.
Bring your passport. Since 2024 foreigners must show it on domestic flights, and the name must match the boarding pass.
The Boutique Lounge is open to all Bangkok Airways passengers, with free snacks, drinks and Wi-Fi. The Blue Ribbon lounge is for Business Class.
The Boutique Lounge is free for all Bangkok Airways passengers, also in economy. At Phuket it is in the domestic terminal, 2nd floor, near Gate 4, open 05:30-21:30 (Nov 2025).

items.setup: Install. The free version is enough.
items.cost: Free. Silver and Gold are paid upgrades.
tips: Tap the HKT airport icon for arrivals, departures and delays.
Point your phone at a plane in the sky to see which flight it is.

items.name: Google Maps
items.what: Main map and navigation. Download offline areas at home, because signal is weak on boats, in the hills and at jungle parties.
items.where: All of Thailand. Offline maps give driving routes only: no walking routes and no traffic offline.
items.setup: On Wi-Fi: profile picture > Offline maps > Select your own map. Download Phuket, Koh Samui and Koh Phangan. Save your hotels, venues and the piers.
items.cost: Free.
tips: To download: tap your profile picture > Offline maps > Select your own map, move the box, then tap Download.
Offline you get driving directions only: no walking or transit directions and no traffic. Use Organic Maps to walk offline.
Google updates offline maps on Wi-Fi before they expire. Turn on 'Auto-update offline maps' in the Offline maps settings.
Save your hotels and party venues, and show the pin to drivers.
Offline maps expire. Turn on Offline maps > Settings > Auto-update offline maps.
Share live location: profile picture > Location sharing > New share. People without Google get a link that works up to 24 hours.
Save places: open a place, tap Save and pick a list. Make one list per island.
Show the map pin to drivers; Thai addresses are hard to say.

You can import and record routes.

items.name: Wise
items.what: Card and app that pays abroad at the mid-market rate plus a small fee. Use it for card payments in malls, hotels and Grab, and for cash from Thai ATMs.
items.where: Anywhere Visa or Mastercard is taken: Phuket, Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Phuket airport. Cash works at any Thai bank ATM, also on Koh Phangan.
items.cost: Free account. Card 7 GBP or 7 EUR (9 USD in the US). Changing to THB costs about 0.6-0.75% from GBP, EUR or USD (Wise prices, 16 Oct 2026). ATM: free up to 250 GBP/EUR/USD a month, then 2.69% (UK, Ireland) or 1.95 USD + 1.95% (US).
items.setup: Open the account, verify your ID and order the plastic card early, because delivery takes some days. Add the card to Apple Pay or Google Wallet. Top up before you fly.
tips: Thai ATMs add their own fee: 250 baht with Visa, 350 baht with Mastercard (Kasikorn, SCB, Krungsri, GSB, 2026). Take out larger amounts.
Wise cards from Ireland and the EEA are Visa, so the Thai ATM fee is 250 baht. The network depends on the country of your card, so check yours.
If the ATM or card machine offers your home currency, say no and choose THB. The Wise rate is better.
The Wise app can pay Alipay+ QR codes (about 1.8-1.9% in total, Oct 2026), but not Thai PromptPay QR yet. Not for Wise accounts from the US, Canada or Japan.
Wise can also send baht to a Thai bank account, for example for a villa or tour deposit.

Thai ATMs still charge their own fee for each withdrawal with a foreign card: 250 baht (Visa) or 350 baht (Mastercard) at the big banks in 2026. The card does not pay it back, so take out bigger amounts less often, and choose baht if the screen offers your home currency.
items.verification: 16 Oct 2026: Wise card fee pages for UK, IE and US (ATM free to 250, then 2.69% or 1.95 USD + 1.95%; card 7 GBP, 7 EUR, 9 USD). items.name: Revolut
items.what: Card and app like Wise. Change money to baht in the app, then pay by card or take cash at Thai ATMs. Take Wise or Revolut; you do not need both.
items.where: Anywhere Visa or Mastercard is taken: Phuket, Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Phuket airport. Cash works at any Thai bank ATM.
items.cost: Free Standard plan (UK and EU, Oct 2026): exchange up to 1,000 GBP or EUR a month with no extra fee, then 1%; 1% extra at weekends; free ATM up to 200 GBP or EUR or 5 withdrawals a month, then 2%.
items.setup: Order the card early and add it to Apple Pay or Google Wallet. Check 'Your plan' or 'Your limits' in the app for your free limits. Change some money to THB on a weekday.
tips: Standard plan: exchanges from Friday 17:00 to Sunday 18:00 New York time cost 1% more. In Thailand in January that is Saturday 05:00 to Monday 06:00.
Plus plan: 0.5% weekend fee. Premium, Metal and Ultra: no weekend fee and a higher free ATM amount (Premium UK: 400 GBP a month).
The Thai ATM fee (250 baht Visa, 350 baht Mastercard) comes on top. Take out larger amounts.
If a card machine offers your home currency, say no and pay in THB.

Thai ATMs still charge their own fee for each withdrawal with a foreign card: 250 baht (Visa) or 350 baht (Mastercard) at the big banks in 2026. The card does not pay it back, so take out bigger amounts less often, and choose baht if the screen offers your home currency.

items.name: Apple Pay (Wallet app) / Google Wallet
items.what: Pay with your phone, using your foreign card, at card machines that take contactless payments.
items.where: Card machines with the contactless symbol: malls, 7-Eleven, hotels and bigger restaurants in Phuket, Samui and Koh Phangan. Markets, street food, small bars and taxis usually want cash or Thai QR.
items.cost: No fee from Apple or Google. Your card's normal rate and fees apply.
items.setup: Add your Wise, Revolut or bank card to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet at home. Your bank may send a code to your home number.
tips: Thailand is not on Apple Pay's country list, so Thai bank cards cannot be added. Your foreign card still works where the machine shows the contactless symbol.
7-Eleven takes cards and phone payments only from 200 baht. Pay smaller amounts in cash.
Apple says some machines show the symbol but are not set up for contactless. Then use the plastic card or cash.
If the machine offers your home currency, choose THB.
